transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-21
Start: 16:30 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes (per calendar)
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Nora Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Kaur (Redwood CSM); Marta Reyes (Procurement), Samir Gupta (CISO), Dana Brooks (Legal), Evan Lin (AI Platform)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be noisy):
Quick procurement gatecall to confirm MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, pricing worksheet approvals, and next steps for vendor onboarding. Security asked for SOC2, subprocessor list, KMS workflows, and jurisdiction. Procurement needs pricing approval and insurance numbers for vendor gate. Redwood to send redline and bench results.

Topics covered:
- MSA redlines and key DPA clauses (data retention, deletion, subprocessors)
- SLA targets, uptime and credits, incident response
- Pricing: hosted vs dedicated vs private (Reserved capacity) and approval timeline
- Security artifacts: SOC2, penetration test, KMS/HSM, VPC/private deployments
- Onboarding timeline and procurement gating checklist

Transcript: (timestamps approximate, transcription not perfect)
[00:00] Liam Chen: Alright thanks everybody for joining, uh this is Liam from Redwood Inference, um with Nora on the call as our solutions engineer and Priya from CSM — appreciate you all making time for what I expect to be a fairly focused gatecall.
[00:34] Marta Reyes: Hi team, thanks. We just want to make sure procurement has what we need to move Redwood through vendor approval, specifically MSA redline, DPA, insurance, and the pricing numbers for our finance committee.
[01:08] Liam Chen: Totally. We've prepped a marked-up MSA that addresses standard points — indemnity, limitation of liability, data protection — and Nora will walk through the DPA highlights. We'll send the documents after the call.
[01:45] Nora Alvarez: Quick note — we may have some auto-transcription hiccups, but on the DPA side the big ones are data residency, deletion on termination, subprocessors, and audit rights. We can support both hosted and private deployments, and for Private we provide a customer-managed control plane option.
[02:22] Samir Gupta: When you say private, do you mean full on-prem or VPC peering in our cloud? We have a requirement for no egress to third-party storage for certain PHI workloads.
[02:56] Nora Alvarez: Good question. We have VPC Peering for Private where compute sits in your VPC and logs can be routed to your SIEM. For air-gapped / on-prem we offer an on-prem package but that usually has a longer lead time and separate commercial terms. Egress can be restricted and KMS integration is supported.
[03:30] Dana Brooks: From legal: we need to see the subprocessors list, SOC2 Type II report, and an indemnity cap that aligns with our policy. Also audit rights — we prefer on-site audit or a third-party attest.
[04:05] Liam Chen: Understood. We'll provide SOC2, third-party pentest summary, and a current subprocessor list. On indemnity and liability we can discuss redlines; our standard positions are in the MSA, but we're open to discussing carveouts for PHI with tighter terms.
[04:40] Evan Lin: For the SLA — what uptime do you commit to for hosted and for Dedicated? Our bar is usually 99.95 for prod.
[05:10] Nora Alvarez: Hosted: typical target is 99.9 with credits for outages; Dedicated (reserved capacity) is designed for higher SLOs and we can discuss 99.95 or contractual SLA with an elevated support tier. There's a tradeoff on cost.
[05:42] Samir Gupta: Ok, so we need explicit numbers in the contract and an incident response time — say 15 minutes for Sev1 acknowledgement and a runbook.
[06:18] Priya Kaur: We'll include our escalation matrix. For Dedicated customers we offer faster on-call response and optional on-site engineering for critical incidents as part of a premium SLA.
[06:54] Marta Reyes: On procurement process: we need a single pricing worksheet that shows recurring costs, tiering for tokens/embeddings, and a Reserved capacity quote with commitment levels. Also any one-time onboarding fees.
[07:30] Liam Chen: We'll send a breakdown: hosted per-token, embeddings per-unit, and dedicated reserved instance pricing with monthly commit options. We can also include a conservative forecast template for the finance team.
[08:05] Dana Brooks: Insurance — we need limits on cyber liability and proof of E&O. Minimums are standard with our vendors; we'll send you the procurement playbook excerpt.
[08:40] Samir Gupta: A question on data deletion — we require strong deletion guarantees and ability to demonstrate deletion from backups within 30 days of request. How does Redwood handle model logging and KV cache?
[09:12] Nora Alvarez: We have configurable retention windows — logs, prompts, and KV cache can be kept for X days by default and we can shorten that. For Private deployments data stays in your VPC. For hosted there's an option to opt-out of storing prompts beyond ephemeral processing; DPA will specify retention and deletion timelines. Backups are included in the DPA, and we will surface the process for deletion requests.
[09:50] Evan Lin: Are your embeddings reversible or hashed? We need to understand re-identification risk for PII.
[10:20] Nora Alvarez: Embeddings are numeric vectors — not reversible. We can also apply additional encryption at rest and customer-managed KMS so keys are controlled by you. Re-identification risk is low but will note it in the security supplement.
[10:55] Marta Reyes: Procurement also flags vendor risk assessment — do you have a FedRAMP or targeted compliance?
[11:24] Liam Chen: We don't have FedRAMP out of the box; our common attestations are SOC2 Type II, ISO mappings, and we provide pen test summaries. We're increasingly supporting regional requirements and can work with partners for more regulated workloads.
[11:58] Dana Brooks: On jurisdiction — we prefer CA or NY law; do you have a preferred venue?
[12:26] Liam Chen: Our standard is California law, venue San Francisco, but it's something our legal team can discuss. We often see customers negotiate venue to their home state.
[12:52] Samir Gupta: Let's talk pricing allowances for benchmarking. If we run a proof-of-concept, will Redwood provide credits or discounted pilot pricing? That affects finance sign-off.
[13:28] Liam Chen: Yes, pilot credits are common. For POC we typically include a credit pool or temporary discounted rate while we run benchmarks. Nora will run a small benchmark and share numbers.
[13:58] Nora Alvarez: I'll run a 4-hour benchmark for their typical prompt mix and one 8k-context run — results will include p99 latency and cost per 1k tokens. Note: real-world latencies vary with prompt shape and kv-cache hits.
[14:35] Evan Lin: On model variants — if quality regressions happen, how do you support rollbacks and A/B testing?
[15:03] Nora Alvarez: We support model pinning, canary deploys, and automatic fallback policies. Our Console shows per-route metrics so you can compare output quality and token costs.
[15:38] Marta Reyes: For procurement checklist, one more item — we need a list of subprocessors and any third-party managed services (e.g., monitoring, SSO providers).
[16:10] Liam Chen: We'll provide a current subprocessor list and indicate which are critical. We'll also note where customers can opt for self-hosted equivalents for certain components.
[16:45] Dana Brooks: A specific legal ask — we might want to add a clause limiting Redwood from using customer prompts for model training. Is that in the DPA?
[17:10] Nora Alvarez: Yes, we can specify usage limitations in the DPA. Our standard is not to use customer prompts for training absent explicit opt-in; we'll make that explicit in the redline.
[17:40] Samir Gupta: On encryption — customer-managed KMS keys? HSM?
[18:05] Nora Alvarez: We support KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and can discuss HSM-backed keys for higher assurance. For hosted customers you can supply keys for at-rest encryption of customer artifacts.
[18:40] Priya Kaur: Also worth noting: audit logs and token-level billing are available in the Console which procurement likes to see for chargebacks.
[19:12] Marta Reyes: Sorry, quick interruption — our procurement committee will also need a runbook for offboarding. What does on/off boarding look like?
[19:43] Liam Chen: Offboarding includes a documented data deletion timeline, certificate revocation for any federated access, and a final invoice. We'll include a checklist in the vendor onboarding package.
[20:12] Evan Lin: Slightly technical — if we choose Dedicated, can we pin GPU type and quantization profiles for cost predictability?
[20:40] Nora Alvarez: Yes, Dedicated lets you choose node types and we can recommend quant profiles. Redwood Optimize also gives recommended quantization and batching settings for typical workloads.
[21:12] Dana Brooks: We'll need explicit SLAs for performance degradation too, not just availability — e.g., when you move us between variants that increase latency.
[21:42] Liam Chen: Good point — we can include SLOs and a performance regression clause tied to fallback policies. We'll draft language that ties credits to measurable p99/p95 deviations.
[22:10] Samir Gupta: Procurement often wants a 90-day exit window without penalty in the contract for new vendors; how does that map to reserved capacity?
[22:40] Liam Chen: Reserved capacity usually has commitment terms; we can propose a staged approach — start with hosted pilot with a 90-day review and if you convert to Dedicated, that's a separate contract with commitments. We'll call that out in the commercial proposal for flexibility.
[23:12] Marta Reyes: And one more compliance question — can you provide data handling diagrams and network flow for our security review?
[23:40] Nora Alvarez: Absolutely. We'll upload a network diagram, data flow, and a mapping of where data resides for each deployment model.
[24:10] Dana Brooks: From the legal lens — we want limitation of liability carveouts for gross negligence, and also a warranty that you comply with applicable privacy laws. Also need to define subprocessor notification windows.
[24:42] Liam Chen: We'll take notes and propose language. Typically subprocessor notification is 30 days and a posted list that we update.
[25:10] Evan Lin: Can we get a copy of your run-of-the-mill SOC2 report redacted? Our security team wants to review controls for vendor gating.
[25:40] Liam Chen: We'll share a SOC2 Type II report under NDA if needed or via our shared portal. We'll include the pen test executive summary.
[26:12] Samir Gupta: A small risk detail — do you use any third-party LLM hosts or is the inference all in-house on your runtime?
[26:40] Nora Alvarez: Our serving runtime is our infra and we run optimized kernels on GPU fleets. We don't proxy to other LLM hosts for generation; model variants are either third-party open models we host or our verified variants.
[27:10] Marta Reyes: Procurement wants to understand onboarding time — how long from PO to production?
[27:40] Priya Kaur: Typical hosted onboarding is days to a couple of weeks. Dedicated provisioning can be 4–6 weeks depending on capacity and network setup; private/on-prem longer. We'll include a timeline in the onboarding packet.
[28:12] Dana Brooks: For DPA retention windows, we need explicit numbers — 30 days, 90 days? What's standard?
[28:40] Nora Alvarez: Our defaults are 30 days for ephemeral logs, 90 days for extended telemetry by default. But those are configurable per-contract. We'll put those in the DPA draft.
[29:12] Liam Chen: I'll recap — Redwood will: send redlined MSA/DPA, SOC2 and pen test summary, subprocessor list, pricing worksheet, and onboarding checklist. Nora will run benchmarks. Priya will assemble onboarding timeline and support SLAs. 
[29:52] Samir Gupta: Sounds good. On pricing, can you highlight cancellable commitments and any minimum spend?
[30:20] Liam Chen: We'll show tiered commitment levels and clearly mark minimums; pilot credit will be separate line item to offset initial evaluation.
[30:55] Marta Reyes: There may also be a procurement gate for vendor risk which includes cyber insurance certificates and financials; we'll submit a formal vendor questionnaire.
[31:25] Liam Chen: We'll provide the insurance certs and financial snapshot.
[31:55] Dana Brooks: One last contract note — data exportability on termination. We want machine-readable export in 30 days.
[32:25] Nora Alvarez: We'll include an export process and timing in the MSA/DPA.
[32:55] Evan Lin: Are there examples of customers with similar compliance needs? Case studies?
[33:25] Liam Chen: We have anonymized case studies for healthcare-tier customers; we'll share a redacted case study if helpful.
[33:55] Priya Kaur: Also, the Console supports token-level cost breakdown per route which helps internal chargebacks. We'll demo that in the next session.
[34:25] Marta Reyes: Ok, procurement will need the pricing and insurance first for initial approval, legal will prioritize MSA redline after that.
[34:58] Dana Brooks: We'll aim to review initial redline within 3 business days once received.
[35:25] Liam Chen: Perfect. Any blockers we haven't covered?
[35:54] Samir Gupta: Just to confirm — if we require HSM-backed keys, what's the lead time?
[36:20] Nora Alvarez: HSM or custom KMS integration can add configuration and contract time — usually 2–4 weeks depending on the provider. We'll quantify in the note.
[36:50] Evan Lin: For Dedicated, will you provide a performance SLA that includes p99 and p95?
[37:20] Nora Alvarez: We can include p95/p99 targets in a dedicated SLA and tie credits to deviations; we'll propose concrete numbers in the SLA draft.
[37:50] Marta Reyes: A quick doc share request — please upload the procurement playbook items and pricing worksheet to our shared drive and ping procurement.
[38:20] Liam Chen: Will do. Link note: Redwood security packet and SOC2 — we will upload to the shared SSO portal (link to be sent).
[38:50] Dana Brooks: One more legal flag — termination for convenience vs termination for cause. Some of our stakeholders ask for shorter notice periods for termination for convenience.
[39:20] Liam Chen: We'll flag termination windows in the redline and call out differences between hosted pilots and committed Dedicated contracts.
[39:55] Priya Kaur: Operationally, onboarding checklist will include IAM/SAML config, VPC peering steps, and contact points for escalation. We'll attach that.
[40:25] Samir Gupta: Regarding subprocessor notification, 30 days is ok but we may want the ability to object to certain additions.
[40:53] Nora Alvarez: Standard is notice, with an objection window; we'll add language for high-risk subprocessors that triggers review.
[41:20] Marta Reyes: For pricing approvals, we'll need a single point of contact from Redwood for invoice and procurement comms.
[41:48] Liam Chen: That's me — I'll be the procurement point. Priya will be the onboarding POC.
[42:15] Dana Brooks: Ok. Anything else?
[42:40] Evan Lin: Can you also share a sample SLA and redline template we can preview?
[43:05] Liam Chen: Yes, we'll include a sample SLA and the MSA/DPA redline.
[43:35] Nora Alvarez: I'll start the benchmark and attach the results with p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens. Expect the sheet by Tues 2025-10-28.
[44:05] Priya Kaur: We'll also prepare a short onboarding timeline PDF — sending by 2025-10-24.
[44:35] Marta Reyes: Procurement will collate everything and present to the finance committee; expect follow-up questions.
[45:02] Liam Chen: Understood. We'll make materials concise and annotated for procurement reviewers.
[45:30] Dana Brooks: We'll aim to have legal feedback to you within a week of receiving the redline.
[45:58] Samir Gupta: Anything on export controls or data processing agreements w.r.t. EU data?
[46:25] Nora Alvarez: For EU data we support regional deployments and can accommodate data residency. DPA will detail cross-border transfer mechanisms.
[46:55] Evan Lin: If we go forward with Dedicated, can we schedule a technical deep dive on network topology and peering?
[47:25] Nora Alvarez: Yes — propose a 60-90 minute technical session with our infra team; we'll schedule with Evan and Samir.
[47:55] Marta Reyes: Great. Procurement will expect the final pricing worksheet and insurance certs to proceed to approval.
[48:20] Liam Chen: We'll prioritize those items. I'll recap final deliverables and owners in an email after the call.
[48:50] Priya Kaur: Thanks everyone — we'll attach the onboarding checklist and sample SLA in the follow-up.
[49:20] Dana Brooks: Thanks, talk soon.
[49:50] Liam Chen: Appreciate it, we'll follow up with the redline and packet. Meeting end.
